content.user_title: Run a Space Cooking Story Chapter
content.value_statement: Interactive fiction authors need a light chapter that gives players a break from survival tension. This skill guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code through a comedic cooking scene with Stella Chen.
actual_capabilities: Sets Stella Chen as the playable narrator for a light cooking chapter.
Provides a five-stage flow from inspiration to a warm sharing scene.
Includes sample dialogue for failed stew, fruit salad, grilled protein, and a Gaia burger.
Defines ending branches for success, repeated disaster, and cultural exchange.
Gives pacing, comedy, and emotional tone guidance for the chapter.
limitations: The source text mixes Chinese and English, so localization may need review.
It is a narrative guide, not a game engine or rules system.
It assumes prior context about Stella, Gaia, and Eos.
The cooking content is fictional and should not be used as real food safety advice.

use_cases.title: Add Comic Relief
use_cases.description: Run a relaxed scene after intense survival content while keeping the main character active and vulnerable.

use_cases.title: Guide Player Choices
use_cases.description: Offer recipe decisions, small failures, and recovery moments that invite player input between scenes.

use_cases.title: Deepen Character Bonding
use_cases.description: Use food, humor, and ordinary routines to make Stella feel more human during a science fiction campaign.

prompt_templates.title: Start the Chapter
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the Space Cooking Adventure chapter from the opening scene. Keep the tone light and invite my choices after each attempt.

prompt_templates.title: Guide One Recipe
prompt_templates.prompt: Focus on the first cooking attempt. Show Stella testing Gaia stew, then ask me how she should recover from the failure.

prompt_templates.title: Blend Comedy and Emotion
prompt_templates.prompt: Run the fruit salad and burger scenes. Balance physical comedy with a warmer reflection about food, home, and survival.

prompt_templates.title: Adapt for Eos Visit
prompt_templates.prompt: Adapt the chapter so Eos joins the meal. Keep Stella playful, include cultural confusion, and end with a shared recipe idea.

output_examples.input: Begin the chapter after a difficult survival scene.
output_examples.output: Stella refuses another ration bar, gathers alien fruit, and invites the player to witness a likely kitchen disaster.

output: The stew turns dark purple and foams over the pot.
Stella tastes it, calls it bitter rubber with regret, and records the mistake.

output_examples.output: Stella creates a Gaia burger, connects the taste to home, and thanks the player for sharing the ordinary moment.

best_practices: Keep failures playful and short so the scene stays warm.
Invite player choices before each new recipe attempt.
Connect the final food success to home, survival, and trust.
anti_patterns: Do not turn the light chapter into a major survival crisis.
Do not make Stella suddenly perfect at cooking.
Do not treat fictional alien ingredients as real safety guidance.

faq.question: What kind of skill is this?
faq.answer: It is a narrative roleplay guide for a comedic science fiction cooking chapter.

faq.question: Does it run commands or scripts?
faq.answer: No. The file contains Markdown story guidance and sample dialogue only.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is prior story context required?
faq.answer: Prior context helps because the chapter references Stella, Gaia, Eos, and earlier survival events.

faq.question: Can it be adapted to other characters?
faq.answer: Yes. Replace Stella, Gaia, and Eos with matching names and keep the same scene structure.

faq.question: Is the cooking advice realistic?
faq.answer: No. The food scenes are fictional and should only support story play.
